title: Oil Change
summary: Maintenance blueprint for checking oil condition, interval history, filter access, and leak evidence before completing an oil and filter service.
symptoms: Service interval or maintenance reminder due
Dark, diluted, low, or contaminated engine oil
Oil seepage around drain plug, filter, housing, or pan
Engine noise, low oil level, or history of oil consumption
inspect_first: Mileage and time since last oil service
Oil level, color, fuel smell, sludge, coolant contamination, and metal debris
Drain plug, pan threads, filter housing, cooler seals, and visible leak paths
Correct oil viscosity, capacity, filter type, and reset procedure
repair_overview: Confirm service interval, oil specification, capacity, and filter style.
Inspect oil level and condition before draining so problems are not hidden by fresh oil.
Drain oil, replace drain plug washer when required, and replace the oil filter.
Refill with correct oil, run the engine, check for leaks, and verify oil level.
Reset maintenance reminder when applicable and document any leak or contamination concerns.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong oil viscosity or filter application
Missing a damaged drain plug, overtightened plug, or old filter gasket
Resetting the reminder without confirming level and leak status
Ignoring sludge, coolant, fuel dilution, or metal debris found during service
estimate_guidance: Use the correct oil type, capacity, and filter style for the vehicle.
Note leaks, damaged drain plug threads, or filter housing seepage before final approval.
Do not turn oil service into leak repair unless inspection supports the added work.
Mention maintenance interval context so the quote reads as preventive service, not diagnosis.

specialty: Torque wrench for drain plug where required

recommended_repairs.title: Oil Leak Inspection
recommended_repairs.description: Use when oil residue, low level, or customer complaint suggests an active leak.
